transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Kendrick Lowe (Redwood CSM); Dr. Lena Ortiz (Everwake CTO), Marcus Bell (Everwake Head of MLOps), Sofia Ramos (Everwake Procurement), Ivan Cho (Everwake Infra)

Summary:
- Renewal conversation focused on adding capacity for a sustained uptick and activating EU region plus VPC/private option for a subset of PII workloads.
- Action: Redwood to provide tiered pricing, bench numbers for long sequences, and a short canary/fallback runbook.

Topics: renewal term length, capacity uplift (reserved vs burst), EU region onboarding, private/VPC segmentation, security certs (SOC2 + encryption/KMS), latency vs cost trade-offs.

00:00 Jordan: all right, hey everyone, thanks for coming today, um this is Jordan from Redwood. I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll walk through the ask, and then Priya will go over the perf plan.
00:22 Lena: hi, thanks. We're on a bit of a crunch here, so appreciate it.
00:28 Marcus: yeah, quick context — we've moved the recommender into prod last quarter and saw usage grow faster than expected, so the renewal is kinda tied to capacity and a potential EU activation.
00:40 Jordan: totally, congrats on the rollout — that's great. So goal today is to align on target QPS, whether reserved capacity or burst is better, and VPC/private constraints for PHI-ish workloads.
00:56 Priya: and I'll talk bench plan — we wanna show both hosted and dedicated numbers for your profile. I'll also cover kv cache behavior with long seqs, and quantization options.
01:12 Ivan: small note, our security team wants to make sure anything with patient identifiers stays in our VPC region in Ireland.
01:21 Jordan: yep understood. We can do a split model — public hosted for non-sensitive traffic and a private VPC lane for PII. There's a couple ways to handle that, we'll propose both.
01:33 Sofia: procurement question — if we move to dedicated, what's the typical commitment window? Is there any flexibility?
01:41 Jordan: standard is 12 month reserved, but we have 6-month pilots and burst credits; we can propose a hybrid with a 9-month step-up if that's helpful.
01:55 Marcus: the key for us is predictability during peak ETL runs — we need throughput guarantees for a 4 hour window daily.
02:06 Priya: ok can you share the typical peak numbers? avg qps?
02:12 Marcus: at baseline 120 qps avg, spikes to ~700 qps for four hours, payloads ~1.2 to 2.1 KB, median seq len ~512 but tail up to 2k tokens for certain chains.
02:30 Priya: great that's exactly what we need. We'll size bins for 512 and 2048 to show per-token cost.

05:04 Jordan: quick commercial — we can do commitment tiers that automatically scale up with predictable unit costs, and then separate note for private hosting premium.
05:24 Lena: on the private hosting cost: is that mostly node licensing or network egress?
05:31 Kendrick: there's a split — private deployments include a platform fee plus infra; egress mostly depends on your cloud arrangement. We can provide a detailed TCO breakdown.
05:45 Marcus: important: we need KMS integration, and HSM ideally for keys, or at least customer-managed KMS.
05:52 Priya: we support customer KMS and can integrate via your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM; we'll note the exact specs in the security pack.

08:10 Sofia: timeline — procurement wants to know when we'd need a PO to make Sept 1 activation.
08:17 Jordan: rough math: PO by 8/20 for Sept 1 is tight but doable for hosted and dedicated baseline; private VPC may need more lead time, say 4-6 weeks after PO for network and certing.
08:33 Sofia: ok we'll try for 8/18 then.

12:00 Priya: bench plan overview — I'll run continuous batching and KV cache warm/unwarm scenarios, long sequence runs at 512/1024/2048 tokens, and will capture p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec. Also I'll compare int8 quantized runners vs fp16 for throughput.
12:24 Marcus: and please include cold-start for KV cache invalidation — we saw a big latency hit when we rolled last week.
12:30 Priya: yep will simulate cache misses, warmups, and prefix reuse.

15:00 Jordan: the other ask was EU residency. Do you need EU-only models or just EU compute region?
15:10 Lena: compute in EU and logs/data retention in EU for the PII pipeline; for non-sensitive stuff we can stay in US.
15:18 Jordan: ok, we can map a route policy: route PII to EU private cluster, rest to hosted in US. We'll include the config snippet.

18:45 Marcus: curious about failover — if EU pool spikes or goes down, do we fail open to US? That's a no-go for PII.
18:53 Priya: right — we have per-route policies that can be configured to block or fail silently; for PII we can set strict NO-FALLBACK and for non-sensitive set graceful fallback. We'll send the policy example.
19:10 Ivan: what about latency SLOs for EU — we need p95 < 200ms for 512 tokens at 100 qps.
19:18 Priya: for dedicated GPUs in eu-west with batching tuned we'd be able to hit that for 512; for 2k seqs p95 will be higher, we'll surface exact numbers in the bench.

23:05 Jordan: competitively, we know Nimbus offers a similar private path; Marcus, were you evaluating them?
23:12 Marcus: yes they were in the bakeoff. Their pricing looked lower for burst but their SLAs weren't great. Also we liked Redwood's observability console.
23:26 Jordan: good to hear. We'll highlight difference in the proposal.

28:00 Priya: let's go through a quick checklist for what I'll need to run benches — Marcus: prod request profile, a few representative prompts, expected concurrency distribution, and access to a staging key if possible.
28:16 Marcus: ok I'll drop the profile into the shared folder after this.
28:21 Jordan: note for procurement — we'll include a clause for early termination for regulatory reasons and an audit log retention add-on.

31:40 Sofia: on SOC2 and certs — we need SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 summary, plus HIPAA BAAs for the patient flows.
31:51 Kendrick: yep we can provide SOC2 Type II report and a BAA template; HIPAA support is standard for private lanes. We'll attach docs.

35:10 Lena: for run-of-prod test, can Redwood run a pilot inside our VPC for one week to validate end-to-end?
35:20 Jordan: yes, we typically do a 5-10 day pilot for private on-ramp. We'll coordinate with Ivan on networking.
35:31 Ivan: FYI our security team prefers using their own KMS keys for the pilot, is that workable?
35:37 Priya: yes, customer-managed keys for the pilot are fine; we'll need IAM policies and a short cert checklist.

39:02 Marcus: question on quantization — will int8 materially change output quality for our models? We have sensitivity in scoring.
39:10 Priya: usually for classification/regression tasks int8 is fine; for highly sensitive prompt completions we recommend evals. We'll run a qualitative eval set you provide.
39:24 Marcus: ok we'll give a 200-sample eval set.

44:05 Jordan: commercial ask — if you commit to 12 months at X tokens/month we can include a 10% on-prem setup credit and a discounted private lane. I'll put numbers in the proposal.
44:18 Sofia: would that discount apply if we need a 6-month initial pilot then convert to 12 months?
44:24 Jordan: yes, we can do credit that offsets pilot, then start the reserved term on conversion. We'll spell it out.

48:30 Kendrick: wrap up — recap of next steps and owners. I'll send the readout doc and action item list after the call.
48:40 Lena: thanks, this was helpful.
48:45 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pricing and bench schedule.
49:02 (crosstalk) Marcus: thanks all.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — "K V cash" for KV cache, "V P C" spaced out, and a couple names flagged differently by the auto transcriber. This is a medium-quality transcript and some timestamps are approximate.
